title: #9 - Sending Troops At Every Turn Is Really Barbaric
content:
#9 - Sending Troops At Every Turn Is Really Barbaric

Chapter 9 Sending troops at every turn is too barbaric

At noon on the second day, Stonehedge.

Like Arthur's family, the flag flying over Stonehedge is also a red horse with a golden shield.

The three of them traveled for half the night last night, rested on the road for half the night, and galloped all the way in the morning, and finally arrived at Stonehedge.

For some reason, Arthur was not very anxious.

He even had the leisure to consider the pattern of his own flag.

The red horse of the Bracken family fits the theme of riding, and if there is a pattern of slashing, it will be in line with his wishes.

Arthur is thinking about whether to add a machete to the flag.

But there is no rush for this, and we still have to wait until the reinforcements are relieved.

There are not many highlands in the riverlands, and Stonehedge is also built on a mound.

But unlike Arthur's family, Stonehedge is much larger.

Like Riverrun, Raventree, Seareach, and the Twins, it was one of the few strong castles that was not taken down by Tywin's Westerly Army in the early days of the War of the Five Kings.

Although only Riverrun and the Twins in the north held out until Robb led the Northern Army to rescue.

But this does show the solidity of Stonehedge.

Arthur thought of this and suddenly felt that he should consider the direction of development.

It is known that Robert has taken Eddard Stark south and has not returned to King's Landing.

And there were about three or four months between Robert's southward journey and the Little Devil's return from the Wall and his capture in the Riverlands.

During this period, the Little Devil, Jon Snow, and Benjen Stark went north to the Wall, the great emperor Joffrey sent people to assassinate the unconscious Bran, and the wolf mother Catelyn went south to report the news, etc. Many small things that affected the situation happened.

Stannis's escape back to Dragonstone, the Lion Lannisters' determination to make progress, and the Rose family becoming the man behind the three deer Renly Silberbine, etc., have greatly influenced the future of Westeros.

It is impossible to go out and enjoy yourself. There will be great turmoil in Westeros in the future.

Now there is no turmoil, Arthur's own money can be stolen by servants who have known him for more than ten years and served him for decades. If he really went to King's Landing, White Harbor and other places to avoid the war, he might be cheated out of everything.

You know, neither the original owner nor Li Hao in the previous life has ever been mixed up in society.

It is better to stay in your own territory honestly.

At least in your own territory, Arthur is a local emperor.

What's more, there is a Mount and Blade system. If he develops better, he can make a name for himself in the War of the Five Kings.

Chaos is a ladder!

And he is a nobleman in the riverlands, so the camp is already very clear.

The camp of Tully of the Fish Family and Stark of the Wolf Family.

In his previous life, he watched Game of Thrones and felt very sad about the fate of the Wolf family.

Although Robb's killing of Karstark and the wolf mother Catelyn's private release of Jaime were speechless, they were not punishable by death.

In fact, the younger generations of the Wolf family, Sansa, Jon, and Arya, are all very good people.

Sansa spoke up for Dontos and saved his life when she was in danger. Arya even remembered the death of Mycah, the son of the butcher. Jon did not discriminate against Sam like other black-clad Night's Watchmen, etc.

Even Robb's killing of Karstark had a reasonable reason.

Two Lannister branch children were killed for no reason after being captured, and the leader of the hostile force was willing to stand up for the two dead people.

Although this matter is very pedantic, it shows that Robb treats people equally.

Like his father Ned, pedantic to the point of being annoying, but not annoying.

Because they have sentient beings in their eyes.

There is another reason to join the Wolf and Fish camp-Edmure Tully, the Three Rivers Archer God.

A true archer god who hits the target with one shot!

How bad can a person's character be if he lets his subjects enter his castle to avoid the war and is criticized by others for a lot of useless words?

While thinking, the horses' hooves have climbed up the hill and arrived in front of the Stone Fence.

Eight soldiers stood in front of the gate. Seeing the arrival of the people, the captain of the guards shouted: "Please dismount, sir."

Arthur and the other two dismounted, and two soldiers came to lead the horses away.

"You are Lord Arthur Bracken, right? May I ask if you have an invitation from Lord Genos or Miss Jayne?" The captain of the guards walked up and asked.

"No." Arthur said anxiously, "I have a big business with Earl Genos, and I need to see him now."

Although he came to ask for help, the statement had to be changed.

It is safer to use interests to drive Genos to send troops.

With Brynden in his hands, he could at least get a ransom of several thousand gold dragons. If he gave half to Janos, he would be happy to step forward.

"But Lord Janos is not here. He went to Riverrun." The captain of the guards replied.

"Then find Hendry."

Hendry Bracken is Lord Janos's nephew and the earl's favorite heir.

Because the earl has five daughters and no son.

According to seniority, Hendry is Arthur's cousin.

Because Hendry has the sponsorship of his uncle Lord Janos, he often travels to various places in Westeros, so he doesn't meet the original owner, a otaku, very often.

The relationship is not very familiar.

But everyone has the surname Bracken, and they are also rare families with ancestral blood in the south. It should be no problem to persuade Hendry to send troops.

"Lord Hendry is in the martial arts field behind the castle. Please follow this guard." After the captain said, he designated a guard to lead the way.

Arthur and the other two followed.

In fact, the way of entertaining guests in Stonehedge City is a bit impolite.

If a noble comes to visit, at least Arthur should be invited to the living room of the castle, and then Hendry should come out to entertain him.

But maybe the captain of the guard knows the details of Arthur's family, or there may be other reasons, so it is not so particular.

This is also good, saving a lot of red tape.

…

"You mean, let my family send troops to help you out, and then blackmail an earl?"

In the martial arts arena, Hendry sat on a luxurious chair, crossed his legs and said.

Beside him, there was a large group of noble children.

On the left and right sat Carel Vance and Mark Piper.

The former is the heir of the Vance family in the city of Journey, and the latter is the eldest son of Earl Clermont of the Piper family in the city of Pink.

The three people sitting are the first heirs of the leading noble families in the riverland.

The people around included free knights, sworn knights, small nobles, and the second sons of big families.

Arthur came at an unlucky time and ran into a group of nobles preparing to go hunting.

After listening to Arthur's request, Hendry disagreed (did not think it was correct).

"We are a family. Now that I have the opportunity to make a fortune, how can I forget your family?" Arthur replied.

"Who is a family with you, a small noble with only nine small villages in the same territory?" The three people sitting did not speak, but one of them spoke first.

Obviously, the words of nine villages made these nobles find fun, and some people began to laugh.

Others were holding back their laughter. But Arthur believed that as long as one of the three people sitting laughed, the rest would laugh.

Hendry didn't laugh at his relatives. "Arthur, your proposal is really uncivilized. You always send troops to fight. You are just as barbaric as the Doraskes. Otherwise, I will send someone to tell the Blackwoods that you are just joking. You release the people and they withdraw the troops. How about that?"

This proposal is impossible. The family savings are lost. Without the money exchanged for Brynden, how can he arm his own people?

Arthur rolled his eyes and suddenly thought of an idea.
